steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. What are three strategies for reducing carbon emissions in cities?

steps.action:
1. Electrify and decarbonize urban transportation  
   • Expand reliable, high-frequency public transit; add dedicated bus lanes and light-rail corridors.  
   • Build extensive, safe cycling and walking infrastructure to cut short car trips.  
   • Accelerate the switch to zero-emission vehicles (buses, taxis, ride-shares, municipal fleets) while powering charging stations with renewable electricity.

2. Retrofit buildings for energy efficiency and clean heating/cooling  
   • Mandate stringent building-performance standards and offer incentives for insulation, high-efficiency windows, and smart energy management systems.  
   • Replace fossil-fuel boilers with electric heat pumps or district heating that uses waste heat and renewables.  
   • Require on-site or rooftop solar where feasible and procure 100 % renewable power for municipal buildings.

3. Embed low-carbon planning and green infrastructure in urban design  
   • Zone for dense, mixed-use neighborhoods so residents live near jobs, services, and transit, reducing travel demand.  
   • Preserve and expand urban green spaces, street trees, and green roofs to absorb CO₂, lower the urban heat island effect, and cut energy use.  
   • Implement circular-economy practices—city-wide waste reduction, composting, and local material reuse—to curb emissions from landfills and long supply chains.
